# National Survey of Family Growth: agent index

A survey of US men and women aged 15-49 about family life, marriage and divorce, pregnancy, infertility, contraception, and health. Released in cycles; cycle 12 is 2022-2023.

Publisher: National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), CDC. Dataset id: `nsfg`. Records follow PublicDataToolkit standard 0.1.

Terms: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/policy/data-user-agreement.html. LLM processing: `allowed`.

Dimensions: `wave` is the cycle.

## How the shards are organized

Every shard is the result of a filter over the records, and its header says which filter and what completeness label it supports. Each shard comes in two forms with the same variables: `.txt`, one line per variable, for scanning; and `.jsonl`, the full records with corrections applied, for details. The first JSONL line is the shard's header (`{"shard": ...}`); every later line is a variable. A shard too big to read at once (about 20,000 tokens) is split into parts.

Line form: `name | waves; forms | scale signature | label | question text`. A run like `1972-1978` means every wave of the release in that span; a gap between runs (`1972-1985,1987-2024`) means the variable wasn't available in the waves between, even though the release has them. The release's waves are: `2022-2023`: 2022-2023. `forms A,C` lists every form the variable was on in any wave; the JSONL `availability` gives wave by form. A trailing `*` on a name means a field was corrected.

Read `SKILL.md` before answering a question from these files.
